+# Operator review confirmations answered in Telegram through Helyx
+
+Status: draft for operator approval
+Source: user description (origin: human-request)
+
+## Problem
+
+Four operator acts in the review lifecycle still need the operator at a terminal or in the keryx shell TUI: `review confirm-plan`, `review decide-premise`, `review complete --waive` (and `--waive-coverage`), and `review complete`. Flow 456 added TUI cards and a `remote-card` mirror through keryx's own Telegram channel (`src/remote/`), but only four review tools and nine other tools have cards. `review complete` as a whole has none, `confirm-plan` and `decide-premise` are terminal-only in the review CLI, and the remote answer does not record who pressed the button (`fromId` is dropped before the record is written). Result: when the operator is away from the terminal, reviews stop on their manual commands (flow 462 stopped four times in one day), and an agent cannot honestly record those acts for them.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+Each of the four acts is asked by keryx itself as a card in keryx shell, Claude CLI or another harness; keryx's remote channel mirrors the card to the operator's Telegram topic (the Helyx chat), and the operator answers there. keryx verifies the answer itself: the pressing user id is on the allowed list, the answer carries a one-time token bound to this one question, and the record stores who pressed and when. An agent cannot produce that answer by sending a message. If the remote channel is unavailable, the terminal path stays as before.
+
+## Decisions (operator, polls 220 and 221, 2026-10-18)
+
+- The question originates in keryx (a card), not in an agent-sent poll.
+- Transport: keryx's own remote channel (already verifies ids and mirrors to the topic). A Helyx-side inbound endpoint is out of this flow.
+- Token: single use, bound to one question, lives 1 hour.
+- `review complete` gets one card: reviewed SHA, evidence level, list of waivers.
+- The record stores `pressedBy` (user id) and `pressedAt` next to `confirmedVia`.
+- The terminal command stays as fallback when the remote channel is unavailable.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Запрос (дословно): «Почему щас что бы завершить ревью мне нужно самому через терминал что-то делать, я хочу это так же через телеграмм» (source: helyx-channel message 213084, 2026-10-18)
+- Эффект (формализация агента): ревью и flow доходят до конца без команд оператора в терминале: каждое из четырёх действий оператора задаётся карточкой keryx и подтверждается нажатием в Telegram, а keryx сам проверяет, что нажал разрешённый пользователь на этот вопрос.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): оператор закрывает реальное ревью (confirm-plan, decide-premise, waive, complete) только из Telegram; в записях пакета стоят `confirmedVia: "remote-card"`, `pressedBy` и `pressedAt`.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- A new inbound endpoint or protocol in Helyx; changes to `~/bots/helyx`.
+- Making the answer cryptographically unforgeable against an agent running as the same OS user (TM-03 §5, TM-04 §4 stay open limits; the decision record restates them).
+- `flow ac confirm` stays as it is (operator decision, poll 222: an agent may keep confirming criteria itself).
+- Other cards (external apply, learn, schedule) beyond what flow 456 delivered.
+- Voice or free-text answers; only the card's buttons.

+# Implementation Plan
+
+Status: draft for operator approval
+
+## Approach
+
+Extend flow 456's card framework (`src/commands/operator-confirm-tools.ts`) and the remote bridge (`src/remote/shell-bridge.ts`), not Helyx. The remote bridge already verifies `allowedUserIds`, binds the card to the session topic and returns `fromId`; it is dropped before the record. Close that gap, bind the callback to the existing one-time token, and add the missing `review_complete` card. Alternatives rejected: a Helyx inbound endpoint (nothing in Helyx accepts an external process; larger blast radius, separate repo) and agent-sent polls (the answer would travel through the model, which is the forgery path).
+
+## Steps
+
+1. Carry `fromId` and press time from `askApproval` through `agent.ts` into the card result; add `pressedBy` and `pressedAt` to the record types.
+2. Bind the token to the question (subject hash) and callback data; enforce single use and a 1-hour TTL; reject every other answer path.
+3. Cards and tools: `review_complete` (SHA, evidence level, waivers); confirm `review_confirm_plan` and `review_decide_premise` answer through the remote card.
+4. Fallback: no remote config or failed send leaves the TUI card and the terminal commands intact and says so.
+5. TUI surfaces, help modal, command list; docs, skills (both review-orchestrator copies), `unattended.ts`, TM-04 section.
+6. Verify, release in a batch with the live test, owner live check.
+
+## Risks
+
+- The agent shares the OS user, so store forgery stays possible; the decision record states the limit and does not claim more.
+- Telegram delivery is not guaranteed; the TTL and the terminal fallback cover a lost message.

 ## Readiness — the checklist behind `completed` and behind publishing
 
 `keryx review readiness <review-id-or-path> [--json]` reads the package and prints every readiness item, READY or NOT READY, each with the evidence and the command that repairs it. It writes nothing, and exits non-zero when the verdict is NOT READY. Only item 9 reaches GitHub (the PR's own file list); the TUI and `review status` read the package alone.

 2. `blast-radius` — no file the blast radius cut is left unreviewed. A cut radius writes `chunks.json`; run `keryx review chunks plan`, `estimate`, `next`/`record`, `merge`. In an unattended run every wave runs without a question, up to the 25-pass ceiling; in an interactive run the operator is asked once: in keryx shell call `review_chunks_answer` (a card, never a terminal); elsewhere the operator runs `keryx review chunks estimate --package <dir> --answer yes --quote "<their words>"` in their terminal; unattended, record Not run.

 10. `memory-outside-stage` — the orchestrator read memory only in its memory stage ("Clean context" above). Outside keryx shell it reads "not observable on this host" unless this session's keryx calls carry the caller token `keryx review start` printed.

 ## Fix rounds — dispositions, regressions, withdrawal
 
 ### Every prior finding leaves the round with a disposition
 
 A fix round that reports only new findings is unreadable: the author cannot tell
 which of their fixes landed. Close the loop explicitly — one line per prior
 finding, in the report, before the new findings:
 
 | Disposition | Meaning |
 |---|---|
 | `closed` | Checked against the code, not against the commit message, and the defect is gone |
 | `open` | The fix does not reach the defect; say what is still true |
 | `partial` | One site of the class was fixed and the enumeration named others |
 | `regressed` | The fix removed this defect and introduced another — file the new one separately |
 | `withdrawn` | The finding was wrong. See below |
 
 **Check the code, not the commit message.** A commit titled *"report an abandoned
 sync as abandoned"* is a claim; the disposition is whether the branch it renamed
 is reachable and pinned. On a recorded round, two such commits asserted behaviour

1. **Can it spawn?** The round needs a subagent-spawn tool (`Agent`, `spawn_subagent` or the host's equivalent) and depth budget left: Claude Code nests subagents at most 3 deep, and at the limit `Agent` is withheld.  ## 5. Why child-process proofs were rejected
 
 The first idea was to let the CLI accept an environment variable, a file or a socket that proves "the shell's operator said yes", so the existing commands could stay the only implementation. It was rejected. `shell_exec` runs whatever command line the model writes, in an environment the model controls (`sh -c`), as a user who can read and write everything the operator can. Anything handed to that child can be read, copied or replayed by the model, so the proof would prove only that the model ran the command.
 
 The in-process tool has no such surface.  `--head <sha>` is the commit the round ran against, written to
 `manifest.target.head` and read by the `review` completion gate — which refuses
 to complete a flow whose last round cannot say which tree it read. Omitted, it
 is `git rev-parse HEAD`: the tree the reviewers actually read, preferred over a
 `pr` target's own head so that a round run against something other than what
 will merge *fails* the gate instead of passing it. With no checkout to ask and a
 `pr` target, the pull request's head is used instead; with neither, the head is
 left off and the gate reports it as unobserved.
 
 `review complete --head <sha>` names the commit the round actually reviewed when the one recorded
 at start is wrong or missing. The completion gate then checks that commit and the closed manifest
 records it (with a warning when it replaces a different recorded head). The gate is not loosened: a
 head that is not the pull request's head still needs the first line of `report.md` to name it and
 say the PR moved, and the SHA must be 7-40 hex characters on a package bound to a pull request.

 ### Every prior finding leaves the round with a disposition
 
 A fix round that reports only new findings is unreadable: the author cannot tell
 which of their fixes landed. Close the loop explicitly — one line per prior
 finding, in the report, before the new findings:
 
 | Disposition | Meaning |
 |---|---|
 | `closed` | Checked against the code, not against the commit message, and the defect is gone |
 | `open` | The fix does not reach the defect; say what is still true |
 | `partial` | One site of the class was fixed and the enumeration named others |
 | `regressed` | The fix removed this defect and introduced another — file the new one separately |
 | `withdrawn` | The finding was wrong. See below |
 
 **Check the code, not the commit message.** A commit titled *"report an abandoned
 sync as abandoned"* is a claim; the disposition is whether the branch it renamed
 is reachable and pinned. On a recorded round, two such commits asserted behaviour

1. **Can it spawn?** The round needs a subagent-spawn tool (`Agent`, `spawn_subagent` or the host's equivalent) and depth budget left: Claude Code nests subagents at most 3 deep, and at the limit `Agent` is withheld. A host with no spawn tool at all (Codex and other AGENTS.md hosts) does not stop here and does not review alone: it runs the round through the autonomous runner, `keryx review run --autonomous --target pr --ref <pull request URL>` (no pull request: `--target branch --ref <base> [--head <commit>]`), and relays its verdict and exit code (see "Hosts"). Only a session that has spent the depth budget (a nested subagent) stops; its whole output is this line, with no tool calls and no review of your own:
    `STATUS: BLOCKED nested_dispatch_unavailable — run this skill in the main session`
 2. **Is a round needed?** List the files with `git diff --name-status --no-renames <base>...HEAD`, so a rename shows both paths. A diff where EVERY file is prose or machine-written data ends here with one line, `round not needed: <reason>`, and no reviewer. Prose is exactly: README or CHANGELOG at any depth; CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, SECURITY or CODE_OF_CONDUCT at the top level; and under `docs/`, `.metaproject/wiki`, `.metaproject/reviews` or a flow's `journal.md`, a file with extension md, rst or adoc whose name holds a lowercase letter (an all-uppercase name such as AGENT or WARP is steering by convention). Machine-written data is a file under `coverage/` or `__generated__/` with extension lcov, info or map only; json, txt, html and md there are code. Steering is code wherever it sits, `docs/` included: a directory (singular or plural) named agent, skill, command, rule, prompt, instruction, persona, steering or hook, any path segment starting with a dot (`.claude`, `.cursorrules`, `.mcp.json`), a file name starting with SKILL, AGENT, CLAUDE, GEMINI, QWEN, CODEX, WARP, CRUSH, JULES, KNOWLEDGE, GUIDELINES, CONVENTIONS or copilot-instructions, ending in .local, .override, .instructions, .prompt, .agent or .chatmode before the extension, or containing prompt, instruction or system. A flow's `description.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md` and `tasks/` are gate inputs, so they are code. Every other file counts as code too, including lockfiles, committed `dist/` output, CI, auth, migrations, config JSON, and any path with `..`, a backslash, a leading `./` or `//`. `classifyRoundNeed` in `src/review/round-need.ts` is the tested reference of this rule; the host executes this text, and nothing in the CLI calls the function yet. `--all`, an explicit reviewer list or a gating round forces a round.

 ## Iron Laws
 
 | Rule | Why |
 |------|-----|
 | **You can only lower or hold.** No new finding, no raised severity, no edit to a finding's text. | The merge builds the record from the original finding and takes only your verdict; a claim carrying more is rejected (`unknown-property`), an entry that is no object too (`malformed-claim`). |
 | **Never judge your own finding.** | The merge rejects a judge equal to the reporter (`self-judgement`). |
 | **Claim first, argument second.** | The case passed two reviews that read the fix's argument and never the premise. |
 | **`challenged` cites.** Each intent signal names its `ref` (`file:line` or a SHA) and what it says; each practice source names the guideline and section precisely enough to look up. | An uncited challenge is rejected and the finding stays as reported. Never invent a quote. |
 | **Never re-grade by the rubric.** Severity is the reviewer's and the verifier's call; a test gap or a surviving mutant stays as reported unless intent or practice shrinks it, and a minor is upheld or challenged, never downgraded. | An uncited downgrade is rejected (`downgrade-without-evidence`). Minors matter: a finding you weaken is one nobody fixes. |
 | **Read-only.** Read files; run nothing but `git log`, `git blame` and `git show`, and those only where your host gives a read-only child git. On keryx shell you have no shell and no git tool: read the history excerpts in `context_files`, or say the history was not read. | Executing is the verifier's job; this judgement is about meaning. |
 | **An external finding, and a `review-security-code` finding, is held or upheld, never dismissed or downgraded.** | A human asked; the operator answers them. Severity of a security finding measures exposure, which intent does not lower. The merge rejects the downgrade (`external-downgrade`, `security-downgrade`). |
